hints.title: Reverse Terminal Reachability Obstacle
hints.text: Nodes leading exclusively to terminal nodes are safe, while any path entering a cycle is unsafe. Rather than tracing paths forward from every node, how can reversing directions propagate certainty from terminal nodes backward?

hints.title: Terminal Outdegree Invariant
hints.text: Terminal nodes have an outdegree of zero. Inverting graph directions allows propagating safety backward to any node whose entire set of outbound transitions reaches verified safe targets.

hints.title: Reverse Graph Indegree Elimination Procedure
hints.text: Construct a reversed graph and count the original outgoing edges for each node. Seed an active collection with terminal nodes that have zero outgoing edges. Trace backward through reversed edges, decrementing the original outgoing count for each source. When a source count drops to zero, mark it safe. Return all marked indices in ascending order.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: V: number of nodes in graph
E: total number of directed edges in graph
complexity.notes: Every node and edge is examined once when constructing the reverse graph and once during topological elimination.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Tracing exhaustive paths from each node risks infinite cycle loops or O(V * (V + E)) complexity.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: The reversed adjacency graph and outdegree array take O(V + E) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that terminal nodes have zero outdegree and reversing edges turns cycle detection into Kahn topological sort.
